purpose: Bounded SHED 2024–2025 same-respondent ledger connecting financial-condition paths to persistence and re-entry of consumer adaptations, then to health and unpaid-care paths while preserving dated trigger, remedy, trust, and action as open.

events.date_precision: 2024-to-2025 annual recontact path; no dated bill, price, employer, policy, or household event is identified
events.denominator: 4,419 paired respondents with a valid 2024–2025 financial-condition path and nonmissing 2025 panel weight; adaptation, health, and care denominators vary
events.method: Weighted descriptive SHED panel transition comparison using the 2025 panel weight; no design-based variance or causal estimation
events.missingness: Dated trigger, price or bill, actor, household resources, adaptation reason, schedule control, debt terms, care intensity, remedy, trust, action, switching, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: Respondents moved along worsened, same broad, or improved financial-condition paths between 2024 and 2025 while reporting consumer adaptations in both waves
events.alternatives_before_action: Cheaper products, reduced use, savings, borrowing, family support, work-more, and other substitutes are measured as separate reports but not as a complete feasible-choice set
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Among prior adopters, persistence was higher on worsened than improved paths for switching to cheaper products (86.9% vs 68.8%), reduced use (84.8% vs 66.1%), reduced savings (71.0% vs 55.0%), borrowing (65.1% vs 45.0%), and delayed major purchases (75.2% vs 56.6%)
events.choice_or_response: The same respondents report persistence or re-entry of consumer adaptations; the panel does not identify whether an adaptation protected cash, reduced quality or care, reflected debt, or ended because an alternative became available
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Households and respondents report financial condition and adaptation, but providers, employers, prices, debt contracts, family support, and policy actors that shape practical options are not identified
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: No dated provider, employer, creditor, agency, or firm remedy is linked to the financial path or adaptation
events.durability_followup: Persistence and re-entry are observed descriptively across one annual recontact; longer durability, repayment, buffer restoration, and later security are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Same-respondent adaptation persistence and re-entry are visible across financial-condition paths
events.protected_outcome: Working more, borrowing, using less, or buying cheaper may protect immediate cash flow or consumption; the protected outcome is not directly measured
events.sacrificed_outcome: Time, quality, health, mobility, social participation, savings, future flexibility, and repayment capacity may be sacrificed; the panel does not assign those costs to a named adaptation
events.cost_risk_transfer: Financial pressure can shift risk into borrowing, depleted savings, reduced use, delayed purchases, work time, health, and unpaid care, but the bearer and mechanism are not identified
events.later_outcome: Health direction and unpaid-adult-care entry or exit are observed as adjacent 2025 paths, but treatment continuity, recipient outcome, household recovery, trust, action, switching, and exit are not observed
events.meaning_and_attribution: No respondent-linked attribution, fairness, dignity, institutional trust, cultural meaning, or political judgment is joined to the adaptation path
events.public_or_collective_response: No respondent-linked complaint, organizing, voting, policy demand, or collective response is observed
events.counterexample: Improved financial condition can coexist with persistent borrowing or reduced use, while worsened condition can coexist with ended adaptation, unchanged health, or care exit; broad money recovery is not full-life recovery
events.source_and_uncertainty: Reproduced SHED 2024–2025 same-respondent descriptive panel layers; recontact selection, broad financial categories, no replicate weights, and no dated event limit interpretation

arrows.to: 2025 same-respondent financial-condition path and adaptation persistence or re-entry
arrows.evidence: The recontacted panel uses shared respondent identifiers and reports 2025 adaptation among 2024 prior adopters and re-entry among prior non-adopters, stratified by the 2024–2025 financial-condition path
arrows.counterexample: Annual path categories do not identify a dated trigger, causal direction, or complete household resource trajectory
arrows.remaining_gap: Dated price, bill, income, debt, care, work, or policy event and mechanism

arrows.to: health direction and unpaid-adult-care entry or exit
arrows.evidence: The same paired respondents report health direction and care-status transitions alongside the financial-condition path
arrows.counterexample: Health, family, housing, employment, and care changes can shape both financial condition and adaptation; care status is not care hours or recipient outcome
arrows.remaining_gap: Dated need, care intensity, work/time substitution, treatment continuity, and household attribution

arrows.to: restored material room, quality, health, care, or future flexibility
arrows.evidence: The panel reports adaptation persistence and re-entry but does not observe whether an adaptation protected or sacrificed a defined outcome
arrows.counterexample: Reduced use can protect cash while harming quality or care; borrowing can preserve consumption while increasing future burden
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-respondent protected/sacrificed outcome, amount, time, quality, repayment, and recovery

arrows.to: trust, attribution, civic action, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The SHED adaptation panel layer contains no event-linked trust, blame, institutional response, political action, switching, or exit endpoint
arrows.counterexample: Repeated adaptation can reflect dependence, effective coping, preference, or lack of alternatives; behavior alone does not identify meaning or trust
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-respondent attribution, institutional encounter, remedy, trust, civic action, provider switching, and exit reason

boundary: This ledger formalizes a same-respondent financial-condition-to-adaptation persistence route. It advances the atlas from population adaptation levels to repeated consumer behavior and adjacent health/care paths, but it does not establish a dated cause, remedy, complete recovery, trust change, political action, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact reproduced panel results, denominators, source URL, and interpretation limits are retained; raw SHED files remain outside the repository.
